scope: Live observation of the second-verification (error_code 2046) challenge on the chrome-devtools-mcp Chrome profile, immediately after the user scanned the QR rendered by the official login panel. Only method, path, parameter keys, public constants, field types and the sequence of verify_way identifiers are recorded. No token, ticket, uid, mobile number, nickname, avatar URL or log id is kept.

challengeResponse.data.description: public copy instructing the user to finish verification in the Douyin app before signing in
challengeResponse.data.captcha: empty string (this challenge is not a CAPTCHA)

observedConstants.std_verify_flow_id: the per-login UUID that also appears in the x-tt-passport-verify-portrait header with a .login suffix
observedConstants.std_verify_way: empty in the challenge; the completed method is filled in later
observedConstants.std_verify_token: short-lived per-challenge token, distinct between common_params and biz_params

data.verify_ways.notes: in-app identity verification; flow was auth_multi_panel and scene was mfa
user sends an SMS to a channel number; sms_content arrives as a short literal

challengeResponse.data.schema: sslocal://webview/... deep link carrying the same std_verify_* parameters plus common/global props

followUpEndpoints.source: Read from the live second-verification bundle https://auth.zijieapi.com/ucenter_web/app/second_verification_web/dist/index.umd.production.js (546,885 bytes) rather than from a recording of the calls themselves.

sendCode.data: the caller object with `type` forced to the number 22, then mixed

validateCode.data: the caller object with `type` forced to 22, then mixed

hostSwitch.note: Neither the verify.zijieapi.com host nor the /passport/web/mobile/check_code/ path appears in the earlier login capture, so a native implementation pinned to www.douyin.com would be assuming one of two supported shapes.

followUpEndpoints.mixEncoding: The mixed value is the per-byte XOR 5 hexadecimal form: `type` 22 becomes 3737, and a six-digit code becomes twelve hex characters. This matches the values seen in the earlier recorded requests.

liveCapture.recorderCaveat: The in-page recorder hooks the caller layer, so msToken, a_bogus and x-tt-session-dtrait — which the transport appends afterwards — never appear in these records. Their absence below does NOT mean they are absent on the wire.

validateCode.bodyKeysInOrder: identical to send_code except that is6Digits is replaced by code
validateCode.codeValue: twelve hex characters, the per-byte XOR 5 of the six typed digits
validateCode.note: A successful validate carries only a ticket; the login is not complete until a later poll confirms.

mfaRetryPoll.note: The six ordinary QR fields keep their order and the seven challenge fields are appended, with std_verify_way carrying the method actually completed. This is exactly what douyin_login.rs already builds.
mfaRetryPoll.response: A reissued QR (error_code 0 with a new token and image) rather than confirmed, because the original QR token expired during verification. It is the refreshedQrInPoll shape recorded in the risk fixture, which also re-confirms that fix.

challengeRefired.note: About 88 KB, which is why the 3000-character recorder cap made this response unparseable and why the round-30 challenge census was inconclusive.

liveCapture.confirmedNotObserved: The browser flow did not reach confirmed because the QR expired mid-verification, so that response still rests on the earlier fixture.

followUpEndpoints.status: RECAPTURED LIVE. send_code, validate_code, the challenge re-fire and the biz_params retry poll were all observed directly; see liveCapture.

crossCheckAgainstEarlierCapture.why: The repository already ships apps/tauri/test/fixtures/douyin-login-capture.json from an earlier session. Because stale captures were explicitly called out as a risk, this round compared its claims against today's independent observation instead of trusting it.
independentlyConfirmed: The check_qrconnect request body field set and order (need_logo, is_frontier, token, is_new_login, next, need_short_url) matches today's live request byte for byte, including next carrying no trailing slash.

The poll query carries the QR SDK constants (passport_jssdk_version 3.4.9, passport_jssdk_type normal, is_from_ttaccountsdk, aid 6383, language, account_app_language, ts, is_from_iesaccountsaas) exactly as recorded earlier.
The p_ui / p_ca / p_ca_real / p_js_* / p_zt / p_ver* / p_bd / request_host metadata block is present on the poll, as recorded earlier.

The 2046 response key set matches the earlier responseShape exactly: account_flow, biz_params, captcha, common_params, desc_url, description, encrypt_uid, error_code, event_params, extra_params, pack_verify_way, passport_scene, schema, url, user_info, verify_scene_desc, verify_ways.

The three verify_way identifiers and their per-way field lists match the earlier record: face_verify (auth_ticket/avatar_url/cert_app_id/flow/identity_name/is_auth_verify/nick_name/scene), mobile_sms_verify (act_type/mobile), mobile_up_sms_verify (channel_mobile/mobile/sms_content).
The multi-way challenge genuinely occurs: this account was offered all three, so the earlier record was not describing a single-account quirk.
notConfirmedToday: SUPERSEDED for send_code and validate_code: both were recaptured live later in the session, see followUpEndpoints.liveCapture. The two SMS shapes now have two independent sources and agree.
SUPERSEDED for the biz_params retry poll: its request shape was captured live; only its confirmed response is still single-source, because the QR expired mid-verification.
The earlier claim that is_new_login appears only in the QR-generation query and only in the check form was still not re-derived from today's samples.
crossCheckAgainstEarlierCapture.verdict: For the QR challenge and its 2046 payload, the earlier fixture is corroborated by independent live evidence and can be relied on. The post-challenge SMS calls remain single-source and should be re-observed before any implementation depends on their details.

outstanding: send_code and validate_code were not re-observed; their form and query contract still rests on the earlier capture in douyin-login-capture.json.
The final check_qrconnect retry that appends biz_params and returns confirmed was not re-observed.
Which verify_way a given account is offered varies: this account exposed all three, while the earlier capture exercised mobile_sms_verify only.
